citation: Hoque et al. TLR9 and the NLRP3 Inflammasome Link Acinar Cell Death With Inflammation in Acute Pancreatitis
model_or_cohort: Caerulein/bile-acid mouse models; genetic and pharmacologic perturbation
main_finding: Acinar-cell DNA/DAMP sensing through TLR9/P2X7-NLRP3-CASP1 links cell death to IL-1beta/IL-18 and pancreatic/lung inflammation.
limitations: Older but foundational; human translation and spatial resolution limited.

citation: Sendler et al. NLRP3 Inflammasome Regulates Development of Systemic Inflammatory Response and Compensatory Anti-Inflammatory Response Syndromes in Mice With Acute Pancreatitis
model_or_cohort: Caerulein/duct-ligation/L-arginine mice; MCC950; human serum context
main_finding: NLRP3/IL-18 drives macrophage inflammation and a parallel Th2/CARS response; MCC950 reduces neutrophils T-cell activation and severity.
limitations: Human biomarker component is supportive rather than a validated diagnostic test.

citation: Zhao et al. STING Signaling Promotes Inflammation in Experimental Acute Pancreatitis
model_or_cohort: Caerulein AP; Cgas/Sting knockout; bone-marrow chimeras; agonist
main_finding: Dying-acinar DNA activates macrophage cGAS-STING-TBK1-IRF3/IFN signaling and worsens AP; knockout is protective.
limitations: Stage- and cell-source-specific; not evidence for routine human STING testing.

citation: Manohar et al. Novel Circulating and Tissue Monocytes as Well as Macrophages in Pancreatitis and Recovery
model_or_cohort: Two AP mouse models; human AP/RAP blood CyTOF
main_finding: Distinct monocyte/macrophage states mark injury, severe disease and recovery; CD206 and CD44/CD54/CD115/CD140a/PDPN-linked states are dynamic.
limitations: Candidate state markers; thresholds and external clinical validation absent.

citation: Wu et al. Macrophage phenotypic switch orchestrates the inflammation and repair/regeneration following acute pancreatitis injury
model_or_cohort: Caerulein time-course mouse AP
main_finding: Macrophages shift from inflammatory to IL4Ralpha-dependent repair with ECM/AKT and metabolic remodeling; supports a continuum rather than fixed M1/M2 lineages.
limitations: Mouse time course; human state mapping incomplete.

citation: Xue et al. Alternatively activated macrophages promote pancreatic fibrosis in chronic pancreatitis
model_or_cohort: Mouse and human CP; IL4Ralpha and IL4/13 perturbation
main_finding: PSC-derived IL-4/IL-13 drives IL4Ralpha-positive AAMs and fibrosis; blockade reduces AAMs and fibrosis.
limitations: AAM labels simplify continuous macrophage states; treatment translation unresolved.

citation: Lee et al. Single-cell sequencing unveils distinct immune microenvironments with CCR6-CCL20 crosstalk in human chronic pancreatitis
model_or_cohort: Human hereditary and idiopathic CP scRNA-seq and scTCR-seq
main_finding: Hereditary CP enriches CCR6-positive CD4 T cells and CCL20-related myeloid crosstalk, whereas idiopathic CP has a different myeloid program.
limitations: Cross-sectional surgery cohort; etiology-specific findings cannot be generalized to all CP.

citation: Zhao et al. STING signalling protects against chronic pancreatitis by modulating Th17 response
model_or_cohort: Experimental CP; Sting knockout/agonist; IL17A blockade; human tissue
main_finding: Unlike AP, STING activation reduces CP inflammation/fibrosis by limiting Th17/IL17A; STING deficiency worsens disease through PSC IL17R-ERK responses.
limitations: Opposite direction from AP is stage-dependent; pharmacologic agonist is preclinical.

citation: Wang et al. Pancreatic Acinar Cells-Derived Sphingosine-1-Phosphate Contributes to Fibrosis of Chronic Pancreatitis via Inducing Autophagy and Activation of Pancreatic Stellate Cells
model_or_cohort: Cerulein and duct-ligation CP; injured acinar cells; PSCs
main_finding: Hypoxia-induced SPHK1/S1P from injured acinar cells activates PSC S1PR2-AMPK/mTOR autophagy and fibrogenesis; PF-543/JTE-013 attenuate fibrosis in mice.
limitations: Human relevance and pharmacologic safety require validation.

citation: Lee et al. Distinct Serum Immune Profiles Define the Spectrum of Acute and Chronic Pancreatitis From the Multicenter Prospective Evaluation of Chronic Pancreatitis for Epidemiologic and Translational Studies (PROCEED) Study
model_or_cohort: PROCEED multicenter serum cohort; Olink 92-plex
main_finding: IL17A/CCL20 and an IL17A-ST1A1 combination distinguish CP-related immune profiles; candidate serum stratification, not an approved test.
limitations: AUC requires independent validation; serum does not localize a niche.

citation: Hagn-Meincke et al. Circulating immune signatures in chronic pancreatitis with and without preceding acute pancreatitis: A pilot study
model_or_cohort: Human cross-sectional CP serum pilot
main_finding: Prior AP in CP is associated with higher IL-6/IL-8/IL-1RA/IL-15 and chemokine signatures, supporting etiologic heterogeneity.
limitations: Pilot sample; exploratory markers without clinical thresholds.

citation: Del Poggetto et al. Epithelial memory of inflammation limits tissue damage while promoting pancreatic tumorigenesis
model_or_cohort: Lineage-traced mouse AP followed by Kras activation
main_finding: Resolved inflammation leaves epithelial memory that accelerates protective ADM on rechallenge but lowers the threshold for Kras-driven tumorigenesis.
limitations: Does not establish the same memory or cancer risk in humans after AP; human longitudinal prevalence and a clinically measurable memory assay remain unproven.

citation: Falvo et al. A reversible epigenetic memory of inflammatory injury controls lineage plasticity and tumor initiation in the mouse pancreas
model_or_cohort: Lineage tracing; scRNA/scATAC/CUT&Tag; mouse pancreas
main_finding: H3K4me1/chromatin memory and reversible MAPK/AP-1 states preserve injury memory and alter later lineage plasticity and tumor initiation.
limitations: Epigenetic memory is not a validated human biomarker; no direct human longitudinal validation, and memory must be separated from active injury.

citation: Carpenter et al. Analysis of Donor Pancreata Defines the Transcriptomic Signature and Microenvironment of Early Neoplastic Lesions
model_or_cohort: Human donor pancreata; scRNA-seq; Visium; multiplex IHC
main_finding: Sporadic PanINs show epithelial and stromal programs, but cell-to-lesion attribution and spatial specificity are limited; immune and fibroblast states differ from PDAC.
limitations: 2D/sparse lesion sampling; donor comorbidities and postmortem design matter.

citation: Zhang et al. Regulatory T-cell Depletion Alters the Tumor Microenvironment and Accelerates Pancreatic Carcinogenesis
model_or_cohort: KC/KPC mice; human PDAC; Treg depletion and CCR1 blockade
main_finding: Treg depletion accelerates carcinogenesis through CCL3/CCL6/CCL8-CCR1 myeloid recruitment, showing that Treg function is context-dependent.
limitations: KC/KPC perturbation is not a clinical recommendation.

citation: Bell et al. PanIN and CAF transitions in pancreatic carcinogenesis revealed with spatial data integration
model_or_cohort: Matched low/high-grade PanIN FFPE spatial transcriptomics integrated with scRNA-seq
main_finding: Maps epithelial and CAF transitions and supports asynchronous, spatially structured progression from PanIN toward PDAC.
limitations: Rare FFPE cohort; spatial spot resolution and cross-sectional design limit causality.

citation: Kiemen et al. Quantitative 3D histology reveals localized immune remodeling during early pancreatic cancer progression
model_or_cohort: >1,000 human precancers; CODA 3D histology; spatial DNA sequencing
main_finding: Immune hotspots and cold spots alternate over tens of microns; higher-grade lesions/duct obstruction show Treg and macrophage-rich hotspots.
limitations: Cross-sectional tissue; 2024 bioRxiv PMID:39149369 is the preprint, not the final publication.

citation: Caronni et al. IL-1β+ macrophages fuel pathogenic inflammation in pancreatic cancer
model_or_cohort: Human scRNA/spatial genomics; functional mouse experiments
main_finding: PGE2 and TNF locally elicit IL1B-positive TAMs that reprogram adjacent tumor cells; PGE2 or IL-1beta blockade reprograms TAMs and controls PDAC in vivo.
limitations: Therapeutic window and patient selection remain untested clinically.

citation: Chao et al. CXCR2-Dependent Accumulation of Tumor-Associated Neutrophils Regulates T-cell Immunity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
model_or_cohort: Human PDAC expression; KPC mouse; CXCR2 genetic inhibition
main_finding: Tumor/stromal CXCL5/CXCL2 recruit neutrophils; CXCR2 loss permits functional T-cell infiltration and suppresses tumor growth.
limitations: Model and ligand distributions differ by species and tumor compartment.

citation: Nywening et al. Targeting both tumour-associated CXCR2+ neutrophils and CCR2+ macrophages disrupts myeloid recruitment and improves chemotherapeutic responses in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
model_or_cohort: PDAC patient blood/tumor; orthotopic mouse; CCR2i/CXCR2i plus chemotherapy
main_finding: Single-axis blockade causes compensatory myeloid influx; dual CCR2/CXCR2 blockade improves antitumor immunity and chemotherapy in mice.
limitations: Preclinical combination; toxicity and patient biomarkers require study.

citation: Bianchi et al. Cell-Autonomous Cxcl1 Sustains Tolerogenic Circuitries and Stromal Inflammation via Neutrophil-Derived TNF in Pancreatic Cancer
model_or_cohort: Human scRNA/IMC; KPC model; CXCL1 silencing/TNFR2 inhibition
main_finding: Tumor CXCL1 recruits CXCR2-positive PMN-MDSC; neutrophil TNF feeds back to tumor/CAF CXCL1, iCAF inflammation and T-cell exclusion.
limitations: High-risk KRAS/TP53 context; generalizability to all PDAC unknown.

citation: Wang et al. Single-cell RNA-seq analysis reveals BHLHE40-driven pro-tumour neutrophils with hyperactivated glycolysis in pancreatic tumour microenvironment
model_or_cohort: Human PDAC scRNA; matched multi-omics; IHC/IF; functional neutrophil studies
main_finding: TANs diverge from blood PMN and acquire BHLHE40-linked glycolysis and TNF/IL1 programs that suppress CD8 function.
limitations: Limited donor numbers and mostly cross-sectional evidence.

citation: Feig et al. Targeting CXCL12 from FAP-expressing carcinoma-associated fibroblasts synergizes with anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer
model_or_cohort: KPC mouse and human tissue; FAP depletion/CXCR4 inhibition
main_finding: FAP-positive CAF-derived CXCL12 excludes T cells from cancer-cell regions; CXCR4 inhibition restores entry and synergizes with PD-L1 blockade.
limitations: Older transplant/autochthonous model; CAF depletion is not equivalent to selective reprogramming.

citation: Biffi et al. IL1-Induced JAK/STAT Signaling Is Antagonized by TGFβ to Shape CAF Heterogeneity in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
model_or_cohort: Organoid, mouse and CAF models
main_finding: IL-1 induces LIF-JAK/STAT and iCAF; TGF-beta downregulates IL1R1 and promotes myCAF, explaining spatial CAF heterogeneity.
limitations: CAF plasticity and target selectivity remain clinically unresolved.

citation: Zhuo et al. A conserved re-epithelialization program underlies malignancy in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
model_or_cohort: Multi-cohort scRNA/spatial/epigenomic and perturbation studies
main_finding: FOSL1-driven MP10 and CTHRC1-high myCAF-EGFR signaling bridge PanIN-to-PDAC invasion.
limitations: Newest study; independent replication and clinical intervention remain needed.

citation: Kinker et al. Mature tertiary lymphoid structures are key niches of tumour-specific immune responses in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas
model_or_cohort: Human scRNA/TCR; multiplex IF; microdissected TLS; TCGA/PRINCE analyses
main_finding: Mature TLSs contain tumor-reactive T cells and are associated with local immune activity and clinical benefit; TLS structure and maturity matter.
limitations: Association is not proof that every TLS is functional or treatment-inducible.

citation: Baer et al. Fibrosis induced by resident macrophages has divergent roles in pancreas inflammatory injury and PDAC
model_or_cohort: Mouse pancreatitis and PDAC; resident macrophage tracing/depletion
main_finding: Resident macrophages support acinar survival and wound-healing fibrosis during pancreatitis but the same fibrosis promotes PDAC progression.
limitations: Human resident-macrophage lineage evidence and therapeutic window remain limited.

citation: Chen et al. Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomics uncover distinct cellular subtypes involved in neural invasion in pancreatic cancer
model_or_cohort: Human PDAC scRNA/snRNA/spatial stratified by neural invasion
main_finding: TGFBI-positive Schwann, NLRP3-positive TAM, myCAF and basal-like malignant cells co-localize in invaded nerves, whereas non-invaded nerves can associate with TLS.
evidence_class: human spatial observational with functional follow-up
limitations: Spatial association does not establish a universal causal neural circuit.

citation: Amo-Aparicio et al. Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Cells Regulate NLRP3 Activation to Generate a Tolerogenic Microenvironment
model_or_cohort: Human cells/tissue; orthotopic FC1242 and KPC mice; OLT1177
main_finding: Tumor CSF1 activates myeloid NLRP3, IL-1beta and COX2/PGE2, favoring Th2 tolerance and reducing CD8 activation; NLRP3 inhibition plus chemotherapy improves control.
limitations: Preclinical drug evidence; exact patient biomarker strategy unresolved.

citation: Elyada et al. Cross-Species Single-Cell Analysis of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Reveals Antigen-Presenting Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts
model_or_cohort: KPC and human single-cell analyses; CAF functional assays
main_finding: Identifies myCAF, iCAF and MHC-II-positive apCAF states; antigen presentation without classic co-stimulation is a candidate CD4-regulatory mechanism.
limitations: MHC-II expression alone cannot prove immunosuppression; causal CD4 outcome needs careful assay.
